brief.news: QuickBooks Online's banking page now autofills payee and category with color-coded review signals (green, blue, orange); Essentials and up add 'Ready to post' batches.
brief.who: Suggestions on all QuickBooks Online versions; Ready to post and Requests for more information on Essentials, Plus and Advanced (US help site).
brief.task: Categorizing and matching bank and card transactions
brief.angle: What each review signal means, which ones to post in a batch and which to open first, how to spot a wrong match or duplicate, and a month-end check that the suggestions didn't drift (compare category totals to last month, then reconcile).

items.title: AI bank reconciliation: how to do it and what AI can’t do
Gemini's new small-business finance tools: what to check

brief.news: Google announced a Gemini business hub that turns spreadsheets, receipts and purchase records into financial charts and models, plus connected apps including Xero and Workspace.
brief.who: All Gemini app users, rolling out globally 'in the coming days' as of Oct 20; confirm it is live before publishing.
brief.task: Turning receipts and spreadsheets into financial summaries and charts
brief.angle: How to give Gemini clean data (an export from your books, not raw bank PDFs), a prompt for a monthly income and expense summary, how to tie every chart total back to your profit and loss report, and what not to upload or connect.

items.title: Can AI do your accounting? What it gets right and wrong
S-corp vs. sole proprietor: when the switch pays off
IRS FIRE is closing: e-file 1099s with IRIS instead

brief.news: The IRS is retiring the FIRE system for information returns; the last day to file through FIRE is Nov. 19, 2026, and tax year 2026 1099s must go through IRIS in the 2027 filing season.
brief.who: Anyone who e-files Forms 1099 themselves (FIRE users must switch). The IRIS Taxpayer Portal is free, takes manual entry or a .csv upload, files up to 100 returns at a time, and needs an IRIS-only TCC (https://www.irs.gov/filing/e-file-information-returns-with-iris, updated 2026-10-22).
brief.task: Filing 1099-NECs and 1099-MISCs for contractors; keeping vendor records (names, TINs, totals) ready
brief.angle: Who this affects (FIRE users, and DIY filers who need a free e-file option), the key dates (Nov. 9 last day to change FIRE TCC applications, Nov. 19 FIRE closes), how to apply for an IRIS TCC now, and an AI prompt that turns a vendor-payments export into rows matching the IRS IRIS CSV template, with a check that each payee total ties to the vendor ledger and no TIN is pasted into a chatbot (mask it, fill it in locally). Re-confirm all dates on irs.gov before publishing; don't state TCC approval times unless the IRS page gives one.

items.title: AI receipt scanning: turn phone photos into bookkeeping records
Google Sheets canvas: build a cash flow what-if tool

brief.news: Gemini in Google Sheets can turn a sheet into an interactive mini-app (Insert > Create a canvas), including financial forecast and scenario models that stay synced with the sheet.
brief.who: Google AI Pro and Ultra personal plans; Workspace Business and Enterprise Standard and Plus; Google AI Pro for Education. Not listed for free Gmail or Business Starter. English only at launch (https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/workspace/sheets-canvas-for-google-sheets-spreadsheets/, 2026-08-13).
brief.task: Cash flow planning: testing what happens to your bank balance if sales, a big expense or a client's late payment changes
brief.angle: Start from a 13-week cash flow sheet built from your real books (opening balance from the reconciled bank account), a prompt that asks canvas for sliders on sales, expenses and payment timing, and checks: the canvas's base case must equal the sheet's totals, and the opening balance must match your last bank reconciliation. Note that a forecast is a planning tool, not a promise, and which plans include canvas. Re-check plan list and click path on Google's pages before publishing.
